sample.headline: Zach Werenski over 2.5 shots is a plus-money coin flip
sample.reason: The case here is mostly the price, not the projection. Zach Werenski's blended rate is 3.23 shots a game, and the Bot projects 2.93 for this one after the game script takes 9.6% off, with CBJ expected to score only 2.455 against CAR. His history supports the over 2.5, with 63.6% of his weighted games landing on this side, and his recent power-play time adds 1.1%. But the fit runs high across all players by 0.084 shots, a warning for an over, and the Bot sits barely above the market. The Book's no-vig chance is 50.49%; the desk bets 50.53% against a 48.5% break-even at +106, so the 1.99-point edge comes almost entirely from the plus-money price.
sample.risk: Since CBJ projects for just 2.455 goals, the script that already cut 9.6% could bite harder and stall him under 2.5, and a 1.99-point edge leaves no cushion.

sample.headline: Sebastian Aho over 2.5 rides the CAR script on a thin price edge
sample.reason: The case rests more on the game script than on the player. His blended rate is 2.73 shots, and with CAR expected to score 3.7 against CBJ the script adds 7.9%, lifting the Bot's projection to 2.92, clear of the line. Against that, only 47.69% of his weighted past games landed over this number, and the fit runs high across all players by 0.084 shots, a quiet warning for an over. His recent average of 3.17 looks supportive, but the Bot gives it no weight. Most of the edge comes from the Book itself: at even money the no-vig chance is already 51.47%, the desk bets 51.5% on over 2.5, and break-even is 50%, an edge of 1.5 points.
sample.risk: If CAR does not dictate play the way its 3.7 expected goals implies, his history under this line takes over, and a 1.5-point edge leaves no cushion.

sample.headline: Under 2.5 shots, with the Book's own price doing most of the work
sample.reason: This edge comes mostly from the Book's own price rather than a bold projection call. The Bot projects 2.3 shots for Steven Stamkos, a hair below the line, off a blended rate of 2.32 across 12 games this season and 82 last, with 62% of his weighted games landing on the under side. The only driver is a league-wide scale at -0.9%, and across all players the fit runs 0.084 shots high, a small tailwind for an under. What the price may be missing is not much: the Bot's 56.24% sits close to the market, so the desk leans almost entirely on the Book here. The Book's no-vig chance for the under 2.5 is 54.53%, and the desk bets 54.59% against a 52.381% break-even, an edge of 2.2 points.
sample.risk: With the projection only 0.2 shots below the line, a routine three-shot night beats this under. The desk also has 111 wins and 120 losses on this bet type and side.
